back: Small, mostly unregistered businesses and self-employed people working outside full regulation, licensing and taxation.
Registered, licensed businesses and organisations that pay taxes, keep records and employ workers on contracts.
Buying goods in a neighbouring country to sell at home, or selling local goods abroad, in small quantities.

front: Give four examples of informal activities in Zimbabwe.
back: Vending, cross-border trading, small-scale manufacturing (e.g. furniture, gates), repairs (e.g. phones, cars, shoes).

front: Which agency publishes official figures on informal employment?
back: ZIMSTAT (Zimbabwe National Statistics Agency), through labour force surveys.

front: Name four characteristics of the informal sector.
back: Small scale; easy entry; mostly unregistered; no contracts or social security (also little capital, cash-based).

front: Name four constraints facing the informal sector.
back: Lack of capital, lack of premises, lack of skills, costly regulation (also no insurance, competition).

front: Why is the informal sector important?
back: It provides jobs and incomes, cheap convenient goods, skills and enterprise, and links with the formal sector.

front: How can councils support informal traders?
back: Build markets with shelter, water and toilets; simplify licences; consult traders' associations.
